page: Google Cloud Platform e2-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance configured with 4 vCPUs and 16 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The underlying hardware features an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor with 2 physical cores and 2 threads per core, operating at a base clock speed of 2.2 GHz. The CPU cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache. This instance type does not include local NVMe storage or bundled GPU accelerators, and it provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations place the e2-standard-4 in the lower performance tiers across most standardized tests. In stress-ng CPU testing, both single-core and multi-core performance fall into the bottom 25% category, with scores of 1105.89 and 2907.35 respectively. Memory bandwidth tests also reflect weak performance, measuring 161.16 GB/sec for cached small blocks and approximately 24.13 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Single-threaded tasks such as gzip compression and bzip3 decompression register in the bottom 10% of tested systems. However, the instance demonstrates average performance in text generation for small 135M parameter language models, achieving 104.71 tokens per second, despite weak prompt processing speeds of 258.44 tokens per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the e2-standard-4 offers a low-cost entry point for workloads that require a balanced resource allocation without demanding high-performance compute or memory throughput. The trade-off for its lower price point is a significant reduction in processing speed and memory bandwidth relative to higher-tier instances. This profile makes the instance suitable for lightweight applications, basic web serving, development environments, and small database operations that do not experience high transaction volumes.
